interest: This document illustrates the wartime displacement and functioning of American diplomatic personnel during the Pacific War, specifically showing Consul General Walter A. Foote and staff from the Batavia consulate operating out of Melbourne following the Japanese invasion of the Netherlands East Indies. It also reflects the U.S. State Department's tracking and indexing of Japanese psychological warfare and propaganda campaigns directed toward Australia during a critical juncture of World War II.
overview: This file consists of a single State Department cross-reference sheet (decimal file 894.20247/4) dated October 26, 1942, which indexes a survey of Japanese propaganda directed toward Australia. The original report was submitted as Despatch No. 4 by American Consul General Walter A. Foote—representing the Batavia consulate while stationed in Melbourne, Australia—and filed under decimal file 894.20200/6. The document connects Japanese wartime military, espionage, and information warfare activities in Australia within the State Department's central decimal filing system.

subfiles.about: Cross-reference sheet indexing a survey of Japanese propaganda directed toward Australia sent by Walter A. Foote from Melbourne.
subfiles.summary: This cross-reference sheet (894.20247/4) records Despatch No. 4 dated October 26, 1942, sent by Consul General Walter A. Foote from Melbourne on behalf of the displaced Batavia consulate. The despatch transmits a survey detailing Japanese propaganda efforts aimed at Australia in the midst of the Pacific War. The note directs researchers to the original paper filed under decimal file 894.20200/6.
subfiles.title: Cross-Reference Sheet for Despatch No. 4 on Japanese Propaganda Directed to Australia
